testingFeedback: 2 critical: the attract demo stalled at the desks and at the pitch; the game did not report hub progress, so the hub harness failed.
The browser run that reads game state after each step, and the AI Hub harness.
The random reel presses: they only confirmed the scoring path, not the timing.
engineFeedback: The standard pause, settings, controls, labels and full screen, plus live portraits in dialogue.
Yes. Prop arguments were in the wrong order, scenes needed their input preset, FlowField ignores map.solid furniture, and the font lacks the middle dot.
The pitch reel, the dialogue state, the attract AI, and the hub progress and result.
Matching the movement input to the view, routing AI around furniture, and carrying flags across scene changes.
FlowField should share the solids grid with the map, so AI routes around furniture without a manual block call.
Scene-entry data should be explicit, and unknown props or actions should fail the build rather than only warn.
promptFeedback: The exact exit-interview shape and the hub tags.
The folder name pattern and the template name differ slightly; the usage line asks for estimates that were not available.
Fitting attract, hub, glyphs, inversion and touch-only into one file under a 1.2 MB engine, and verifying the attract loop.
A headless run with a fake gamepad to check the controller path and the glyph switch, which I could not test here.

aiHub.name: MAD MASTERS
aiHub.description: A 1962 account man at Carrow & Dade gathers three insights, takes a drink or a light, then pitches the Wren to Hollis on a timed reel.
aiHub.controls: Stick or WASD walk, E talk, Shift hurry, M change view, Enter confirm, Escape menu
